gloss: Reading judged: an inductor expert, self or distinct, asymptotically knows its own quotes. For the self-expert this is free: the clean room proves the introspection the scoped theorem needs at grade (a) (concentrates_self, def-argmax-value-report.md item 4), and the landed event smithy-verity-002 put the asymptotic reading near [0.85, 0.97]. For a distinct inductor expert it is an open hypothesis on each arrow of def-squeeze-diamond (report item 3), which is what keeps the lower end at 0.8; nothing suggests it fails for an expert that is itself a logical inductor reading its own published quotes.

Reading judged: P(the deck's first arrow holds | the scoped Lean theorem holds as an implication). If scoped_value is valid as stated (two processes, composite Total Trust, fold, H3), the deck's arrow is the same argument with REGULARITY in H3's place, and the AI reading that REGULARITY is H3 (displayed condition the mass-weighted sum, 'is enough' one-sided) I hold at 0.7-0.9; the arrow rests on that identification, and the slide-19 typo the clean room recorded (def-lattice-arrows F3) is a further small residual, so the conditional takes the identification's range.

Reading judged: P(the deck's first arrow holds | the scoped Lean theorem fails as an implication). Then the Lean evidence is gone, but the slides' own appendix proof (bounds transfer at threshold u = v − ε) and the wiki's prose proof of the theorem (total-trust-implies-value.md, proved modulo the concentration lemma) still stand. Failure of the Lean implication would most likely come from a bridge or completeness defect that the prose shares, so I keep this in the middle, 0.35-0.65.

Reading judged: P(the deck's Value-implies-tower arrow holds, with F4's epsilon-outside patch understood | the forward loop Total Trust ⟹ Value ⟹ Tower ⟹ Total Trust holds). The arrow is one step of that loop, kernel-checked as tower_of_value_probes in def-lattice-arrows, and the probe menus are decided early and so regular; the residual is the patch the slide itself lacks (F4).

Reading judged: the same arrow given that the forward loop fails somewhere. The loop could fail at another arrow (the fold at the ramp, which is prose only) while this one stands, since it has its own kernel check; so the conditional stays fairly high, 0.6-0.85.

Reading judged: P(some non-trivial regular menu sequence exists | FAF's inductor keeps the truth-teller's price frequently interior). def-argmax-value-report.md names truthPrice_frequently_interior as exactly what decides whether a content-bearing instance of H3 exists in its family, so if it holds the premise holds through that family, up to the REGULARITY = H3 identification.

Reading judged: the same premise given that the truth-teller's price is eventually pinned. Then that family gives no witness, but other menu families (benignly correlated menus, which the one-sided H3 was written to admit, total-trust-implies-value.md 'One-sidedness is deliberate') may; nothing has looked, so 0.3-0.6.

Reading judged: nothing beyond the two arrows, REGULARITY and asymptotic self-knowledge is needed. Against: slide 7's chooser is 'argmax with tiebreak', and ledger-decided-tie-breaks.md shows an undecidable tie-break breaks F1 by correlation, so a computable tie-break is an unlisted premise; slide 11 needs the epsilon-outside patch the clean room recorded (def-lattice-arrows F4); the ramp quotes on the composite that scoped_value takes as data (c) are not named on the slides. For: the slides' proofs are short and each step cites what it uses.

Reading judged: the deck's chain as a literal claim, including that non-trivial regular menus exist and that the AI's self-knowledge is asymptotic. The arrows themselves are well supported: the first is the scoped theorem the clean room proved (scoped_value), the second is kernel-checked (tower_of_value_probes). What holds the literal number down is the premise leaf (every known witness of the scoped package is trivial, def-argmax-value-report.md) and the unlisted tie-break premise. As an implication I would put it at 0.6-0.8.

Reading judged: P(H3 holds of the non-trivial menus the theorem is applied to | some natural syntactic menu class larger than the decided and dominance strata makes H3 a theorem). If such a class exists, H3 holds on it by proof and the scoped theorem has content there; the residual is menus outside the class, which a deployment would still face.

Reading judged: the same, given that no natural class makes H3 a theorem. Then H3 is an assumption whose instances must be found one by one; the global form is refuted (condStable_refuted) and the world-only conjecture is refuted as stated (WorldOnlyRefuted.lean, def-argmax-value-report.md State), so 0.2-0.45.

Reading judged: Total Trust of a novice in an inductor expert over the composite bets holds for the pairs the programme is about. The self-expert has it at grade (a) (def-self-trust, the tower and both faces of self-trust), but the scoped_value docstring records that the TotalTrust antecedent's only known inhabitant is the expert itself (N−, diagonal). For a distinct expert this is exactly the open trust question, which the faithful-acceleration results answer only at averaged grades (theoremSS_limitPoint_general), so I stay near the middle.

Reading judged: the concentration statement for an inductor expert. The clean room proves it for the self-expert at grade (a) and from the fold clause in general (def-argmax-value-report.md item 4), with two adversarial audits passed; open-problems.md item 1 calls it the sole remaining gap of hard self-endorsement. The residual is the fold clause for a distinct expert.

Reading judged: the kernel accepts scoped_value as stated. DIGEST.md §1 item 4 reports the axiom audit clean on every gated declaration and the kernel replay of all 1,675 declaring modules passed; def-argmax-value passed its last two fresh-context audits. Residual: I have not replayed it myself.

Both audits sketch a never-losing ramp trader whose existence would make the approach to the limit summable, which is the standard logical-induction shape; a sentence whose truth depends on the inductor's own price being pinned at the boundary would be unusual. Nothing has been attempted, so I keep the range wide.

The world-only conjecture, the obvious candidate, is refuted as stated (WorldOnlyRefuted.lean), which lowers the number; the wiki's hoped-for dichotomy (a menu is either Newcomblike or satisfies Value) still has no counterexample, which keeps it near the middle. Untried since the refutation.

Slide 10 displays the mass-weighted sum with the note that the one-sided inequality is enough, which is H3's one-sided mass-weighted form, and the deck file dates from 2026-07-27, a day after that form was written. Reading judged: the same route given the deck's chain fails as an implication. Then the scoped direction would need a different scope condition than the deck's, which is possible (invalid toys can still be improved), but the scoped Lean theorem would also be in doubt, so 0.1-0.3.

Reading judged: the route as a whole. The deck's chain is well supported as an implication (scoped_value; tower_of_value_probes), so the derived number is driven by the distinct-expert transport and by non-vacuity, both open; I read it near the derived mixture.

Reading judged: P(the hedged collapse holds for a human and a distinct AI inductor | hedgedValue_of_totalTrust holds as an implication). The implication is general (two processes) in the ledger; what remains is Total Trust over the composite for a distinct expert, which is the deference hypothesis, and the composite's ramp quotes for a non-paper expert.

Reading judged: the same route given hedged Value fails as an implication. The route would then need another softening; I keep it low but not negligible because the soft-argmax idea is not tied to this one statement.

Reading judged: the hedged route as a whole. Its implication is kernel-checked and its bill is the smallest of the routes (no tie-break, no conditional-stability, survives punishing menus, soft-self-endorsement.md); the open part is the same deference hypothesis every route needs.

Reading judged: P(a policy-level collapse exists | the toy collapse holds as an implication). The policy-level route aims to bypass the argmax and its selection problem; the toy's validity would show the epistemic arrows compose, which helps a policy-level version somewhat. The page itself says 'It is not known whether this is doable'.

Reading judged: the same route given the toy fails as an implication (which its completeness leaves make likely, because Value needs a scope condition). The policy-level route is designed for exactly that failure, so the conditional drops little: 0.2-0.45.

Reading judged: the policy-level route as a whole. No statement attempt exists (the action on policy-level-total-trust proposes one), and the page records that it is not known whether it is doable; it is the one route that bypasses the argmax's selection problem rather than scoping it, which keeps it in play.

Reading judged: P(the transported collapse reflects a human and a distinct AI inductor | the full transport of def-squeeze-diamond holds). With the transport, the collapse holds for a distinct novice up to one hypothesis per arrow; the residual is that the paper's expert read by a distinct process is still far from a human deferring to an AI it trains, and the cross-process tower refutation on quote-referencing families (tracking_fails) bounds the per-day grade.

Reading judged: the same route if the transport fails. Then the self-expert results would not carry to distinct experts in this form; other routes (grades, domains) would have to do the work, so this route's own probability falls to 0.15-0.35.

Reading judged: the distinct-expert route as a whole. Both arrows between Total Trust and the tower already transport with one hypothesis each (def-squeeze-diamond item 3); the Value corner and the conditional tower do not yet. The quote-referencing refutation (tracking_fails) limits how far the pointwise grade can go cross-process.

Reading judged: P(a scheduled-grade collapse reflects a human deferring to a faster AI inductor | scheduled weighted-average Value holds with no scope condition). The conjecture is this route's Value arrow; Theorem SS supplies the trust side at the same grade (theoremSS_limitPoint_general). The residual is whether an averaged guarantee is the trust a deployment needs.

Reading judged: the same route if the Value conjecture fails, for instance because the punishing menu bites every gated day. The scheduled grade would then still carry the epistemic arrows but not Value, so the route falls to 0.15-0.35.

Reading judged: the scheduled-grade route as a whole. The cross-process positive results all sit at averaged or scheduled grades (eisenstat-conjecture-attribution.md §4, 'the averaged/scheduled trust properties were largely proved'), which makes this the route the existing evidence points along; the Value conjecture is untried since 2026-07-31.

Reading judged: P(a quote-free collapse holds for a distinct AI inductor | the toy holds as an implication). The toy's validity helps little: the attribution page records the quote-free tower as underivable with the known tools (the cost-circularity), not refuted.

Reading judged: the same route if the toy fails as an implication. The route's obstacle is the power assumption, which the toy's failure (a scope condition on Value) does not touch, so the conditional is about the same.

Reading judged: the quote-free route as a whole. Its only known proof route needs an unsatisfiable power assumption (attribution §4 item 2), and a collapse restricted to quote-free questions reflects only part of the reality phrase, so I keep it low.

Reading judged: P(an undescribed refinement works out | the toy holds as an implication). The routes filed cover the directions the corpus names (scope, softening, policy level, transport, grade, domain); the residual covers combinations (the alternative information structure of eisenstat-conjecture-attribution.md §2 applied to the collapse, accuracy as the definition of trust) and directions not yet seen.
Reading judged: the same if the toy fails as an implication. The residual barely depends on the toy's literal validity, which is low already through its completeness leaves.

Reading judged: the residual route. It holds the directions the corpus mentions without filing as routes (an accuracy definition of trust, eisenstat-conjecture-attribution.md §2; the information-structure change) plus unknown ones.

Reading judged: the collapse can be improved until it reflects a human deferring to a faster AI inductor it gives feedback to, on questions that may mention the AI's outputs. Four literal refinements are in hand and valid as implications (the deck's chain, scoped_value, hedgedValue_of_totalTrust, Theorem SS at limit-point grade), which the protocol counts as evidence. Against: cross-process, the pointwise tower is refuted on quote-referencing families (tracking_fails), so every route must change the grade or the domain. Four valid refinements put the claim well above even; the bottom stays at 0.6 because every route pays for changing the grade or the domain. The disjunction of the routes under independence comes out higher, which is the structure overstating it.

Feasibility if attempted: two proposed corrections with their Lean names. Both refutations and their surviving neighbours are named in tt-ladder's ledger rows (not_forall_lProdSeq_imp_tSeq; middle_rung_false with tAllEpsSeq_of_lProdSeq_of_supportNondegenerate), so the drafting is short; residual: stating the corrections in the note's own notation.

Reading judged: a first form and statement can be chosen from what exists. Several candidates are complete enough to choose among (the deck, the wiki pages of record, the clean room's checked statements); what could block a choice is that a review may turn up repairs before any is chosen.

Feasibility of drafting the six slides' content, provenance-split, given the deck's chain is valid as an implication. Every slide has a source page: two closing arrows with prose pages, the modest-immodest discussion in reflection-in-li.md, the status summary of the conjecture in eisenstat-conjecture-attribution.md §4; Corrigibility and Legitimacy have the most open content.

Feasibility if the deck's chain fails as an implication: the title-only slides could still be drafted, but the deck's earlier slides would need repair first, and a completed deck resting on a broken chain is not the deliverable's stated property. The repair would follow the clean room's audit of the slides (def-lattice-arrows F3, F4), which names what is wrong. So the deliverable stays possible at roughly even odds.

Feasibility of a provenance-split write-up once the form and statement are chosen. The material exists page by page (the wiki's pages of record, the clean room's digest); the effort is length and the three-way split.

Feasibility without a chosen statement: a draft could state all three candidates side by side, which is a survey rather than the write-up the Statement describes, so lower. A survey is the form crux-first-published-statement's survey picture describes, which is publishable in its own right. The write-up as stated still needs a chosen statement, hence the middle range.

Feasibility of porting and registering, given the pin bump and first port batch exist. The four declarations then have their dependencies available; what remains is the registry's policy on inherited transcriptions (CLAIMS.md) and CI size.

Feasibility without the pin bump: the public tree pins an older FAF on which the clean room's dependencies do not exist, so the deliverable is close to impossible. The clean room's README says moving results into lean/ needs the pin bump and is future work. The residual covers re-proving a declaration on the older pin.

Reading judged: P(the first publication's statement holds as stated | the deck's chain holds as an implication). The deck's chain, the scoped Lean theorem and a survey of notions are close variants; if the deck's chain is valid, whichever of them is chosen very likely holds.

Reading judged: the same if the deck's chain fails as an implication. A survey of notions or the Lean-checked scoped theorem could still be published and hold, but the deck's statement would need repair first, and a review might turn into new research rather than a publication.

Conditional: no policy-level statement exists, so this picture needs new research by definition. The open-problems page records that it is not known whether a policy-level analogue is doable. The small upper end covers a statement attempt that turns out short.

Conditional: a survey can be prepared from the wiki's notion pages and the clean room's lattice (def-lattice-arrows) without new results. deference-notions.md already lists the five notions with their implications, and def-lattice-arrows proves the six-arrow table. Conditional: the talk's six title-only slides can be filled from existing pages (task deck-completion); the Corrigibility and Legitimacy slides are the least settled.

Conditional in the residual picture: some other form (a registered-claims release, a short paper on one arrow). Most such forms reuse results in hand, so the middle-high range; the residual also holds forms that need new research.

The five pictures cover the forms the corpus names; they are close to exclusive because each names one form a first public statement could take, though a talk and a survey can overlap, which the residual and the weights absorb. No other form appears in the corpus. The residual row makes the list exhaustive by construction.

Reading judged: a first published version can be prepared from results in hand. Most of the forms the corpus names need only compilation and review (the talk, the survey, the scoped theorem with its witness question disclosed); only the policy-level picture needs new research by construction.

Conditional: epistemic trust yields a policy-level Value. No statement exists; the page says it is not known whether this is doable.
